chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn reported to me... from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah (may mercy be upon him) who said:
While the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was performing tawaf around the Ka'bah, he came upon a man clinging to the curtains, saying:

"O He Whom one hearing does not distract from another, O He Whom the seekers do not confuse, O He Whom the insistence of the insistent does not weary, grant me the coolness of Your pardon and the sweetness of Your mercy,"

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Is this your supplication?" The man said: "You heard it?" He said: "Yes." The man said: "Then recite it at the end of every prayer, for by Allah, no believer recites it except that Allah forgives his sins, even if they were as numerous as the stars and raindrops, and the pebbles and soil of the earth."

Then the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, I have the knowledge of that, and Allah is Vast, Generous." Then the man, who was al-Khidr (peace be upon him), said: "By Allah, you are right, O Commander of the Faithful. And above every possessor of knowledge is One more knowing."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his pure progeny.

key_terms.إلحاح: Persistent supplication, praised in Islamic tradition
key_terms.الخضر: Al-Khidr, a mysterious immortal prophetic figure who guides the righteous

ai.seo_question: What supplication did al-Khidr teach Imam Ali at the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Mufid recounts an encounter between Imam Ali (AS) and al-Khidr (AS) at the Ka'bah. Al-Khidr was supplicating with a powerful du'a praising God's infinite capacity to hear and respond. He recommended this supplication after every daily prayer, promising complete forgiveness regardless of the number of sins. Imam Ali affirmed his knowledge, and al-Khidr acknowledged Ali's superior status by quoting Quran 12:76.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn reported to me from Abu ‘Ali Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sawli, who reported from Abdul Aziz ibn Yahya al-Jaloodi, who reported from al-Husayn ibn Hameed, who reported from Mukhawwal ibn Ibrahim, who reported from Swaleh ibn Abul Aswad, who reported from Mahfooz ibn Ubaidullah, from a Sheikh from Hadhramaut, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah - may Allah bless him with mercy, who said:
Once, while Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, was going around the Ka’bah , he came across a man who had clung to the curtains of the sacred house, saying:

’O, He, Whom one hearing does not distract from another and O, He, Who is not misled by the seekers, and O, He, Who is not wearied by the insistent supplication. Grant me the coolness of Your Pardon and the sweetness of Your mercy."

Amirul Mu’mineen (A.S.) asked him: "Is this your prayer?" The man said: "So, you heard it?" He said: "Yes". The man said: "Pray this way at the end of every Daily prayer. By Allah, when a faithful prays with these words at the end of the Daily prayer, Allah forgives him all his sins even if they equal the heavenly stars in number, or the pebbles and the earth in abundance."

Then Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, told him: "I have the knowledge of it, and Allah is Infinite, Beneficent." The man who was al-Khidhr, peace be upon him, said: "By Allah, you are right O, Amirul Mu’mineen. Over everyone endowed with knowledge, there is One Who knows most."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet and his pure progeny.
